title: Animation speed
description: Shorter animations make menus feel snappier.

title: Private DNS (ad blocking)
description: Every app's DNS lookups go to this encrypted resolver, which can block ads and trackers TV-wide — no app needed. Free ad-supported apps (Pluto, Tubi) may stop playing with ad blocking on. If the TV says "No internet", choose Default.

title: Limit ad tracking
description: Asks apps not to use your advertising ID for personalized ads.

title: Stop Amazon usage data uploads
description: Turns off Fire OS usage metrics uploads.

title: Surround sound output
description: Send Dolby/DTS straight to your soundbar or receiver. Auto asks the TV what it supports.

title: Stay awake while powered
description: Stops the device dropping the HDMI signal during long downloads or background playback.

title: Screensaver starts after
description: How long the TV waits with no input before the screensaver comes on.

title: Use Aerial Views as screensaver
description: Apple TV-style 4K aerial screensaver. Install Aerial Views from the App store first.

title: Developer options menu
description: Shows or hides the developer options menu in the TV's settings.

title: Fix the clock (Google time server)
description: Use time.google.com if the TV's time drifts or apps complain about certificates.

title: Match content frame rate
description: Switch the TV's refresh rate to match the video (24p films without judder). Android 12+ setting; Google TV and newer Android TV.

title: Remote click sounds
description: Play a click sound when you move around menus.

title: Stop marketing usage data
description: Stop Fire OS sharing app-usage data for marketing (Settings → Preferences → Privacy).

title: HDMI-CEC control
description: Let the TV remote, soundbar and this device control each other over HDMI.

title: Turn the TV on with this device
description: Waking this device also switches the TV on and to its input.

title: Sleep when the TV turns off
description: Put this device to sleep when the TV is switched off.

title: Remove Fire TV tips and tutorials
description: Disables the pop-up tutorials, tips and release-note screens. Re-enable any time.

title: Remove Amazon shopping and news apps
description: Disables Amazon Shop TV, Amazon miniTV and the Fire TV news channel (hedwig).

title: Disable Amazon diagnostics uploads
description: Disables Amazon's wireless metrics collector and diagnostics logger (aria). Can slow down Amazon support troubleshooting.

title: Disable NVIDIA telemetry
description: Disables NVIDIA's stats and feedback reporters on SHIELD.

title: Remove Google TV recommendation rows
description: Disables the service that fills the home screen with recommendations.

title: Keep Wi-Fi on during sleep
description: Wi-Fi stays connected while the TV sleeps, so downloads, updates and casts resume instantly.

title: Skip verification for ADB installs
description: Sideloading via ADB is not re-scanned by the package verifier. Faster installs of large APKs; Play-store installs are still verified.

title: Disable content recognition (ACR)
description: Fire TV stops fingerprinting what's on screen for ads. (firestrip telemetry.py)

title: Disable Amazon Sidewalk
description: The TV stops sharing a small slice of your bandwidth with Amazon's Sidewalk mesh network. (firestrip telemetry.py)

title: Skip Google's internet check
description: Stops the TV pinging Google each time it joins a network. Fixes a false "No internet" warning behind Pi-hole or firewalls that block Google. Downside: hotel/public Wi-Fi sign-in pages won't pop up.

title: Optimize apps now
description: Runs Android's own overnight app optimization immediately, so apps you just installed open faster. Takes a few minutes. Nothing to undo — Android would do this itself eventually.

title: Clear all app caches
description: Deletes every app's temporary cache files to free storage. Logins, settings and downloads are kept; apps rebuild their caches as needed. Nothing to undo.

title: Button Mapper: full access
description: Lets Button Mapper turn on its own accessibility service and unlock all actions — remap Netflix/YouTube/app buttons on any remote. Shown only when Button Mapper is installed. (setup.buttonmapper.app)
check: dumpsys package flar2.homebutton | grep -q 'WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS: granted=true' && echo on

title: tvQuickActions: full access
description: Grants the three permissions tvQuickActions asks for (secure settings, draw over apps, usage access) — the TV-remote clicking you'd otherwise do in its setup. Shown only when it's installed. (tvdevinfo.com docs)
check: dumpsys package dev.vodik7.tvquickactions | grep -q 'WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS: granted=true' && echo on

title: Projectivy: take over the Home button
description: Turns on Projectivy's accessibility service so the Home button opens Projectivy, even on Google TV and Fire TV, which ignore the normal launcher setting. Other accessibility apps stay on. Some TVs (Fire OS, TCL, Hisense) switch it off at every restart: if Home goes back to the stock screen, run this again. Shown only when Projectivy is installed.
check: settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services | grep -q ProjectivyAccessibilityService && echo on
apply: c=com.spocky.projengmenu/com.spocky.projengmenu.services.ProjectivyAccessibilityService; s=$(settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services); case "$s" in *$c*) ;; ''|null) settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services $c ;; *) settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services "$s:$c" ;; esac
undo: s=$(settings get secure enabled_accessibility_services | sed 's#:*com.spocky.projengmenu/[^:]*##; s#^:##'); if [ -z "$s" ] || [ "$s" = null ]; then settings delete secure enabled_accessibility_services; else settings put secure enabled_accessibility_services "$s"; fi
